content_units: Participants:   Product manager, designer, 2 engineers, data analyst, marketing lead
Primary outcomes:   scope alignment, risk review, timeline alignment, clear decision owners
- Open questions reserved for   20 minutes minimum
- Agenda is arranged so marketing input is captured before departure and technical deep-dive starts after the late engineer joins
Phase   Time   Goal   Key Tasks   Deliverable

Opening and working norms   14:00–14:08   Set context and meeting rules   Welcome; objectives; constraints; confirm decision focus; note late/early attendance   Shared understanding of purpose and flow
Project scope framing   14:08–14:20   Align on what is in and out   Problem statement; success metrics; in-scope vs out-of-scope; PM leads   Draft scope boundaries

Market and user lens   14:20–14:30   Capture business and audience context early   Marketing priorities; audience assumptions; launch considerations; analyst adds data signals   Business context and key assumptions logged

Experience and delivery overview   14:30–14:45   Align on solution shape now that all engineers are present   Designer reviews user experience; engineers react on feasibility; PM clarifies trade-offs   Shared concept and feasibility notes
Risks and dependencies   14:45–14:57   Surface major blockers early   Identify delivery, design, data, and stakeholder risks; assign owners to investigate   Prioritized risk list with owners
Timeline and milestones   14:57–15:10   Agree on target phases and checkpoints   Review milestones; key dates; dependency timing; decision deadlines   Draft timeline and milestone alignment

Decision ownership and governance   15:10–15:20   Clarify who decides what before marketing lead exits   List decision domains; assign DRI/owner; escalation path; approval rhythm   Named decision owners and escalation path

Open questions and next steps   15:20–15:30   Resolve top uncertainties and close cleanly   Open Q&A; parking-lot review; recap actions; confirm follow-up artifacts   Action list, unanswered questions, next meeting
- Start exactly on time and acknowledge the attendance constraints up front.
- State the meeting goal in one sentence: “By the end, we will have aligned scope, top risks, timeline direction, and decision owners.”
- Ask everyone to keep comments concise and flag deep-dive topics for the parking lot.
- Note that technical decisions needing both engineers will wait until   14:15  .
- “We’ll optimize the first 30 minutes for cross-functional context.”
- “If something needs more than 2 minutes, I’ll park it and bring it back in Q&A or follow-up.”
- PM should present the project brief in a tight structure:
- Ask the group to validate, not rewrite, the scope.
- Capture any contested scope items in a visible parking lot.
- “What absolutely must be true at launch?”
- “What are we explicitly not solving in this phase?”
- “Is any critical dependency missing from the scope statement?”
- Use this window before the marketing lead’s early exit to pull out:
- Invite the data analyst to anchor assumptions with available evidence.
- “What market or customer timing makes this project urgent?”
- “What assumption would most hurt us if it’s wrong?”
- Once the late engineer has joined, shift into experience and implementation shape.
- Designer should walk through the intended flow or user journey.
- Engineers react on complexity, feasibility, and unknowns.
- Keep this at alignment level; avoid detailed solutioning.
- “Where do we need a spike, prototype, or decision before build starts?”
- Run a fast round-robin so each function names one top risk and one dependency.
- Push for owners, not just concerns.
- “What could delay us most in the next 2–4 weeks?”
- “Which risk needs action now rather than monitoring?”
- “Who owns validating or reducing that risk?”
- Focus on milestone logic, not precise task estimates.
- Confirm any fixed dates, review checkpoints, and handoff windows.
- “What milestones must be visible by next week?”
- “Which dates are fixed, and which are target ranges?”
- “What decision must happen by when to avoid schedule slip?”
- Complete this before the marketing lead exits.
- Define decision owners across the main domains:
- Clarify whether owners are recommenders, approvers, or final decision-makers.
- “Who is the directly responsible owner for each major decision?”
- “What decisions require consultation, and what can be made independently?”

- This preserves the required   20 minutes   for open questions when combined with brief clarifications embedded earlier; if you want a strict uninterrupted 20-minute block, use the alternate agenda below.
- Use a visible list and answer in priority order:
- End with a verbal recap of owners and deadlines.
- “Which question must be answered before work begins?”
- “Let’s leave with owners, dates, and one source of truth.”
Alternate Version With a Full 20-Minute Q&A Block
If you want the open-questions section to be a   single uninterrupted 20-minute block  , use this adjustment:
This version is tighter, but still protects marketing lead participation before   15:20  .
- “We aligned on scope, top risks, milestone direction, and decision owners.”
- “I’ll send notes with actions, owners, and unanswered questions after the meeting.”
- “Anything not resolved today will move into the follow-up decision log.”
headings: Alternate Version With a Full 20-Minute Q&A Block
